newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta shares almost hit all-time high.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta shares almost hit all-time high.

text.p: Active buying almost across the board, including in heavyweight Bank Negara Indonesia, pushed the Jakarta Composite Index near its all-time high at the close on Tuesday.
The Index closed up 6.75 points, or one percent, at 680.88 points, just off the record high of 681.56 points recorded on April 4, 1990.
"Today, the locomotive was Bank Negara Indonesia. Both foreign and local investors bought actively in the stock," a broker with London-based securities house said.
But he doubted if the index could sustain the upward trend on Wednesday with possible profit-taking in a liquid market.
"I just don't feel comfortable with the sharp rises. It's just too fast. I think the market needs to take a breather before setting up for a new rally," another broker said.
In broad market sentiment, gainers led losers by 79 to 49, with 51 counters unchanged. Total volume was 375.8 million shares on a turnover of 671.99 billion rupiah.
The total volume was also boosted by sales of Jakarta International Hotel & Development (JIHD) and Bank Negara Indonesia (BNI) in cross-board.
JIHD cross-traded at 2,245 rupiah on a volume of 20 million shares, while BNI cross-traded at 1,550 rupiah on a volume of 11.5 million shares.

"I see Peregrine did the cross trading on JIHD," a broker with foreign firm said. He said it might possibly be a part of a private placement rumoured since Monday. Company officials were not immediately available for comment.
On the regular board, Bank Negara Indonesia rose 100 rupiah to 1,550 rupiah and topped the active list with 74.5 million shares changing hands.

Brokers said sentiment towards the stock remain high following talks that Morgan Stanley Capital International would include the bank it its index, coupled with expectation that its 1996 earnings would be higher than previously forecast.
Overall market actively was lead by local investors, with limited and selective foreign buying, brokers said.

Sierad Produce, which made its debut on the exchange last December 27, rose 100 rupiah to 925 rupiah on a volume of 58.4 million shares, or slightly above its initial public offering price of 900 rupiah.
Brokers attributed the recovery to reports that the firm and its lead underwriter would be summoned by the Capital Market watchdog for its recent poor performance.
But some said it was undervalued at its present level.
